title: A yearly retreat
tomorrow: does God care which road you walk to pray?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pentecost: a crowded house, every language heard, and one word for the asking: come. Today, a different invitation, and it gets crowded too.

The out-of-office reply is set, the laptop is closed, and then the phone lights up. Mark tells a version of that. Jesus' friends come back from a hard stretch of work, so busy “they had no leisure so much as to eat.” He says, “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while.” They get in a boat. And the crowd runs along the shore and gets there first. The retreat is over before it starts. So why does Jesus let it go?
screen: `NO LEISURE SO MUCH AS TO EAT.` → `COME APART, AND REST.` → `THE CROWD GETS THERE FIRST.`

segments.voice: Mark says what Jesus saw when he stepped out of the boat: he “was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd.” So he teaches them, and by evening the crowd is fed. Here's the strange part, worth telling a friend: the rest wasn't canceled. It was moved. A few verses later, once everyone has gone home, Mark says “he departed into a mountain to pray.” Jesus keeps coming back to it. Mark tells of him “rising up a great while before day” and going out to a solitary place to pray. Luke puts it in one line: “And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.” A desert place, in these stories, means somewhere lonely, out of the traffic. A sabbath and daily prayer are short pauses. A retreat is a longer one: a day, a weekend, set apart to be quiet with God. Christians keep it in different ways. Some stay at a monastery or retreat house and join its rhythm of prayer. Some go with a church group, or meet a guide each day. Some take a quiet day at home, phone off, a Bible open. So the puzzle's answer is a plan: the crowd will always find the boat, so time apart gets put somewhere on purpose, and kept again when it slips.
screen: `MOVED WITH COMPASSION.` · `NOT DROPPED: MOVED.` · `A SOLITARY PLACE, BEFORE DAY.` · `A LONGER PAUSE, MANY WAYS.` · then, large: `COME APART AWHILE.`

segments.voice: Open a calendar, on paper or on your phone, and find one day in the coming months that could be quiet. Mark it, even if it's only a morning, and give it a name you'll recognize. Then spend the rest of the sit as a small rehearsal of that day.
A yearly retreat. Time set apart, a day or more, to be quiet with God, out of the coming and going.
The line to keep: come apart awhile, and if the crowd finds the boat, keep it later. See you tomorrow.
